debrief_steps: Email Hugo asking who in operations owns meter data loads, and attach a one-page load summary he can forward to that person. (owner Mia Torres, due 2026-09-30). Why: Hugo said he doesn't decide and doesn't know who does; AEs may just wait for the summary reply.

Log Kofi's load summary promise with an owner and a send date of 2026-09-30, and tell Hugo when it is sent. (owner Kofi Mensah, due 2026-09-30). Why: No date was given, and passing commitments get dropped; a dated send also lets Hugo forward it.
opponent_steps: Get a named operations stakeholder and an introduction through Hugo** - **Action:** Email Hugo to thank him, then ask for the name of the operations owner of meter data and for a short intro or joint call. Offer to send a 2-line blurb he can forward. Also ask who else signs off on a $120K purchase, and get Hugo's phone number. - **Owner:** Mia Torres - **Timing:** Send within 24 hours (by Sept 30). If there's no reply, follow up by phone or email by Oct 2. - **Why:** Hugo said he doesn't decide and doesn't know who does. The CRM has no champion, no economic buyer and no decision process, so the deal has no path to a decision yet.

Send the load summary with a dated next step attached** - **Action:** Kofi sends the load summary he promised (the 4-minute partitioned load and the regional daily usage view). Mia adds a proposed date and time for a follow-up session, ideally with the operations contact, so the email also asks for a booked meeting. - **Owner:** Kofi Mensah sends the summary. Mia owns the proposed date and the CRM update. - **Timing:** Same day or next morning, with the follow-up session proposed for within about 7 days (by Oct 6). - **Why:** The call ended with only "Sure" and "Thanks," and no dated next step was set. Kofi's summary is the one commitment made, and the dated next step, SC commitment and stakeholder fields in the CRM are all blank.

Re-establish the business outcome and the validation criteria, and re-qualify the deal internally** - **Action:** Mia and Kofi write down what "success" means for the evaluation. The CRM only says "Agreed the TV items" and lists "meter data loads are manual" as a pain, with no stated business outcome. They confirm the outcome and the decision process with the operations contact on the follow-up session. Mia then updates the CRM, flags the single-threaded risk to her manager, and reviews whether the Dec 18 close date is still credible. - **Owner:** Mia Torres leads, with Kofi's input on the validation criteria. - **Timing:** Update the CRM and flag the risk this week. Confirm the outcome and decision process on the follow-up session. - **Why:** The demo showed a load working, but nobody has tied it to an outcome the buyer cares about. Without that, and with only a passive technical contact, the Dec 18 forecast has little behind it.

verdicts.why: B's first step targets the missing operations decision-maker with a forwardable intro and asks who signs, plus dated next step and re-qualification. A is thin hygiene and its first step is partly sound but omits the signer.
A's first step seeks the operations owner, an intro, and who signs, which unblocks the decision. A adds a dated follow-up and re-qualification. B is narrower, with a hygiene-focused second step.
